title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 171
paragraphs: The story of the Rhegians and Tarentines has been a digression in my narrative. In Crete, however, as the men of Praesus relate, after it had been thus stripped of inhabitants, settlements were made by various peoples, but especially by Greeks; and in the second generation after the death of Minos came the Trojan war, in which the Cretans proved not the most contemptible of those who came to help Menelaus. After that, when they had returned home from Troy, famine and plague fell upon both the people and their livestock, until at last Crete was stripped of its inhabitants for the second time, and a third population of Cretans now occupies it together with the survivors of the former. This, then, the Pythia recalled to them and so stopped them from coming to the aid of the Greeks, though they wished to.
